questions.q: She works as ___ engineer at a tech company.
questions.why: Use 'an' before a vowel sound; 'engineer' starts with the /e/ sound.

questions.q: He bought ___ new car last week.
questions.why: Use 'a' before a consonant sound; 'new' begins with the /n/ sound.

questions.q: We had to wait for ___ hour before the doctor saw us.
questions.why: 'Hour' has a silent 'h', so it starts with a vowel sound and takes 'an'.

questions.q: My brother lives in ___ university town in the north.
questions.why: 'University' starts with the /ju:/ sound (a consonant sound), so use 'a'.

questions.q: It will take about ___ hour and a half to get there.
questions.why: The silent 'h' in 'hour' gives a vowel sound, requiring 'an'.

questions.q: She gave me ___ honest answer to my question.
questions.why: 'Honest' has a silent 'h', so the word begins with a vowel sound and takes 'an'.

questions.q: That was ___ useful piece of advice, thank you.
questions.why: 'Useful' begins with the /ju:/ consonant sound, so it takes 'a', not 'an'.

questions.q: He is ___ European tourist visiting for the summer.
questions.why: 'European' starts with the /ju:/ sound, a consonant sound, so use 'a'.

questions.q: The sun is ___ brightest object in our sky.
questions.why: Use 'the' before superlatives because they refer to one unique thing.

questions.q: ___ Earth orbits the sun once a year.
questions.why: Use 'the' for unique objects that there is only one of, like the Earth and the sun.

questions.q: She plays ___ violin beautifully in the orchestra.
questions.why: Use 'the' before musical instruments when talking about playing them.

questions.q: Can you play ___ piano?
questions.why: With the verb 'play' plus an instrument, English uses 'the' (play the piano).

questions.q: ___ water is essential for all living things.
questions.why: Use no article for uncountable nouns spoken about in general.

questions.q: I really enjoy ___ music when I am studying.
questions.why: General uncountable nouns like 'music' take no article when meaning the concept in general.

questions.q: ___ dogs are loyal animals.
questions.why: Use no article with plural nouns used to make general statements.

questions.q: ___ children learn languages faster than adults.
questions.why: Plural nouns making a general statement take the zero article.

questions.q: We are flying to ___ France for our holiday.
questions.why: Most country names take no article (France, Spain, Japan).

questions.q: They sailed across ___ Atlantic Ocean.
questions.why: Use 'the' with names of oceans, seas, and rivers.

questions.q: Have you ever visited ___ United States?
questions.why: Use 'the' with country names that include 'states', 'kingdom', or 'republic'.

questions.q: ___ Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
questions.why: Individual mountain names take no article, unlike mountain ranges (the Alps).

questions.q: It is late, so the kids have already gone to ___ bed.
questions.why: The fixed expression 'go to bed' uses no article.

questions.q: My grandmother is in ___ hospital after her operation.
questions.why: In British English 'in hospital' (as a patient) uses no article.

questions.q: The children go to ___ school every weekday morning.
questions.why: 'Go to school' as an activity (to study) takes no article.

questions.q: I read ___ interesting book about space yesterday.
questions.why: 'Interesting' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

questions.q: He is ___ MP for a town near London.
questions.why: The letter 'M' is pronounced /em/, a vowel sound, so the abbreviation takes 'an'.

questions.q: There was ___ strange noise, and then ___ noise stopped.
questions.why: Use 'a' to introduce something new, then 'the' to refer back to the now-known thing.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She is ___ university student studying biology.'
questions.why: 'University' begins with the /ju:/ consonant sound, so use 'a', not 'an'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I waited for ___ honest answer.' (article only)
questions.why: 'Honest' has a silent 'h', creating a vowel sound that needs 'an'.

questions.q: Type the article or '-' for none: '___ gold is a precious metal.'
questions.why: Uncountable nouns used in a general sense take no article.

questions.q: Type the article or '-' for none: 'We climbed ___ Mont Blanc last year.'
questions.why: Single mountain names take no article.
